verses.english: Those swift ones who carry off the nāga kings,
divine birds, winged, of pure sight,
through the air they came into the middle of the wood.
Citrā and Supaṇṇā — such are their names.
Then there was safety for the nāga kings:
the Buddha made a sanctuary for them from the supaṇṇas.
Calling to one another with gentle words,
nāgas and supaṇṇas alike went to the Buddha for refuge.
Conquered by the one with the thunderbolt in hand, the asuras dwell in the sea.
These brothers of Vāsava are possessed of power and renown.
The Kālakañchas, greatly terrifying, the Dānaveghasa asuras:

verses.pali_roman: Vepacitti sucitti ca pahārādo namucī saha
verses.english: Vepacitti and Sucitti, Pahārāda together with Namucī,
and a hundred sons of Bali, all named Verocana.
Having armed Bali's host, they went up to good Rāhu:
'Now is the time, venerable sir, for the assembly of bhikkhus in the wood.'

verses.pali_roman: Āpo ca devā paṭhavī ca tejo vāyo tadāgamuṃ.
verses.english: The devas of water and of earth, of fire and of air, then came.

verses.pali_roman: Varuṇā vāruṇā devā somo ca yasasā saha.
verses.english: The Varuṇas, the devas of Varuṇa, and Soma together with Yasas.
The hosts of loving-kindness and compassion came, devas of renown.
These ten, tenfold hosts, all of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

verses.pali_roman: Veṇḍū ca devā sahalī ca asamā ca duve yamā.
verses.english: The Veṇḍu devas and the Sahalīs, the Asamas and the two Yamas.
The devas attending on the moon came, with the moon before them.

vocabulary.meaning: the garuda, the great bird that preys on nagas. The opening block is the moment the Buddha makes peace between them
thunderbolt-in-hand — Sakka, who defeated the asuras and drove them into the sea
the titans, rivals of the devas. Named here by their clans: Kalakanchas, Danaveghasas, the sons of Bali
giver-in-former-births, an epithet of Sakka. Page 323 uses it of him again

checks.issue: THE FIRST EIGHT ROWS ARE SINGLE COLUMN, NOT TWO. Measured row by row rather than judged: rows 1-8 carry ink from x 668 to at most x 1397 with no internal gap at any threshold down to 50, while every row from nine on has a clear gutter. This is the only mixed sheet in the roman section, and a page-level gutter scan reports NO columns at all here — which is how it would have been missed.

THE LAYOUT CHANGES WITHOUT A FULL PARAGRAPH BREAK. The vertical gap between the last wide row and the first two-column row is 40px, where breaks inside the two-column part run 80-86px and rows inside the wide block sit 20-37px apart. The gap is ambiguous on its own, so the group boundary here was taken from the LAYOUT change and the bold on 'Jita vajirahatthena', not from the spacing. Recorded because it is the one grouping decision on this sheet that measurement alone does not settle.

The book sets an ELISION APOSTROPHE twice in one line, 'Samayo 'dani, and the line is also enclosed in single quotation marks as reported speech. Kept exactly as printed; a script normalising quotes would change both the elisions and the speech marks.

diacritic_exceptions: varuṇā/vāruṇā — genuinely two different words, and the BOOK prints them SIDE BY SIDE IN ONE LINE. Verse 128 reads 'Varuṇā vāruṇā devā': the first is the Varuṇa devas themselves, the second the adjectival form, those belonging to Varuṇa. Short against long is visible within a single printed row at 5x, so making them agree would erase a distinction the page itself makes. Same reasoning as the va/vā pair on pages 82 and 92.
